title: 419. How to ACTUALLY process your emotions

sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式真的很不一样。

sentences.zh: 我过去真的很专注于做到极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是珍玛·斯派克（Gemma Spake），欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》（The Psychology of Your 20s），在这里我们探讨二十岁时面临的重大变化、时刻和人生转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, let's talk about something I think many of us believe we are doing but probably aren't doing very well, which is processing our emotions.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊一件我想很多人都以为自己做得很好、但实际上可能并没有做好的事情，那就是处理我们的情绪。

sentences.en: This is something that I've come to find.
sentences.zh: 这是我最近发现的一点。

sentences.en: If you are a very self-aware, smart individual of whom I know many of you are and you cry occasionally and you get sad occasionally and you're happy occasionally
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个非常有自我觉察能力、聪明的人——我知道你们当中有很多这样的人——你偶尔会哭，偶尔会难过，偶尔也会快乐，

sentences.en: and you have every word under the sun to explain what it is you're feeling and why, you probably believe that you are someone who processes your emotions well
sentences.zh: 而且你能用天下所有的词汇来解释你究竟在感受什么以及为什么会有这种感受，你大概会认为自己是一个很擅长处理情绪的人，

sentences.en: or who finds that their emotions have a very nice beginning, middle, and end.
sentences.zh: 或者觉得自己的情绪有一个非常美妙的开端、经过和结尾。

sentences.en: You definitely see yourself as somebody who is very emotionally adjusted.
sentences.zh: 你绝对觉得自己是一个情绪非常成熟的人。

sentences.en: Maybe you are.
sentences.zh: 也许你真的是。

sentences.en: But I'm very guilty of this.
sentences.zh: 但我自己在这方面非常内疚。

sentences.en: Just knowing the words for your emotions or just knowing how you think you should be feeling and knowing why you should feel that isn't the same as,
sentences.zh: 仅仅知道描述情绪的词汇，或者仅仅知道你认为自己应该有什么样的感受、知道你为什么应该有这种感觉，并不等于——

sentences.en: A, actually allowing yourself to feel those emotions fully, even in their ugliest form, and B, is not the same as being able to move through those emotions
sentences.zh: 第一，真正让自己充分去感受这些情绪，哪怕它们是最丑陋的形态；第二，这并不等于能够真正穿梭于这些情绪之中，

sentences.en: and move through the discomfort.
sentences.zh: 并且挺过那种不适感。

sentences.en: I think more and more of us, thanks to social media, thanks to just the reduction of stigma, thanks to just education, like we have the language for our emotions
sentences.zh: 我认为，由于社交媒体的普及、污名化的减少以及教育的普及，我们越来越多的人拥有了表达情绪的语言，

sentences.en: without actually having the tools and without actually being able to fully express them, that's meaning we're still kind of feeling emotionally stunted
sentences.zh: 却实际上缺乏相应的工具，也无法完全表达它们，这意味着我们依然在某种程度上感到情感发育受阻，

sentences.en: even though we're very informed.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们见多识广、消息灵通。

sentences.en: That means that without realizing it,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在不知不觉中，

sentences.en: we can become somebody who can't connect with their emotions in a deep way, who can't connect with their emotions without feeling debilitated by them,
sentences.zh: 我们可能会变成那种无法与自己的情绪进行深层连接的人，无法在不被情绪击垮的情况下与之共情，

sentences.en: even though we feel like we should and we do have a good hand over what we're feeling.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们觉得自己应该可以，而且也觉得自己对当下的感受有着很好的掌控。

sentences.en: So that is what we're going to break down today, kind of a guide to the research on why and how we avoid our emotions without consciously realizing it,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们今天要剖析的内容：一份关于研究的指南，探讨我们为什么以及如何在无意识中逃避情绪，

sentences.en: what that actually looks like in our behavior, and in our reactions to things and some of the greatest tools and studies on what to actually do.
sentences.zh: 这在我们的行为和对事物的反应中究竟表现为怎样，以及关于该如何应对的一些绝佳工具和研究成果。

sentences.en: Like what does it mean to process an emotion?
sentences.zh: 比如，处理情绪究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean to be able to cry when you want to cry?
sentences.zh: 想哭的时候能够哭出来意味着什么？

sentences.en: Sing and experience joy when you want to experience joy, be disappointed when you want to be disappointed and I guess like really just exploring why that's actually a gift
sentences.zh: 想体验快乐时就能唱歌并体验快乐，想失望时就能感到失望，我想，这其实是在探究为什么这其实是一种天赋，

sentences.en: and we shouldn't be afraid to process emotions in a way that maybe is a little bit ugly and I guess how we do that in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该害怕以一种可能有点丑陋的方式去处理情绪，以及我们究竟该如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into how to actually process your emotions.
sentences.zh: 那么废话不多说，让我们进入正题，看看如何真正地处理你的情绪。

sentences.en: To begin with, how can we identify when we are becoming detached from our emotions?
sentences.zh: 首先，我们如何识别自己何时开始与情绪产生疏离？

sentences.en: And how can we identify when we are not processing our emotions in a sustainable way?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何识别自己何时没有以一种可持续的方式处理情绪？

sentences.en: Because I think sometimes it's not that obvious, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得有时候这并不是那么明显，对吧？

sentences.en: When we're attached or I'm sorry, detached from our emotions though,
sentences.zh: 不过，当我们与情绪产生疏离时，或者说抱歉，当我们变得冷漠麻木时，

sentences.en: I think things just feel flat.
sentences.zh: 我觉得一切都变得索然无味。

sentences.en: Like we don't feel sad.
sentences.zh: 就像我们不会感到悲伤一样。

sentences.en: We also don't feel happy.
sentences.zh: 我们也不会感到快乐。

sentences.en: I've sometimes like heard this described as like the world is a little bit, it's fuzzy, right?
sentences.zh: 我有时听到有人这样形容：世界变得有点模糊不清了，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't seem to feel your pain in its fullest form, but you also don't feel your happiness in its fullest form either.
sentences.zh: 你似乎无法最完整地感受到你的痛苦，但你也同样无法最完整地感受到你的快乐。

sentences.en: You're like existing in the middle frequency of your feelings.
sentences.zh: 你只是在你的情感的中频区苟延残喘。

sentences.en: Sometimes we're very aware that this is the case and sometimes like, I don't want to say we enjoy it,
sentences.zh: 有时我们非常清楚事实的确如此，有时——我不想说是我们喜欢这样，

sentences.en: but I don't know, we rely on it or we just don't have the capacity to fix this numbness.
sentences.zh: 但怎么说呢，我们依赖这种状态，或者我们根本没有能力去修复这种麻木感。

sentences.en: Like after you've been through a big breakup or you've lost your job or you've had a really traumatic incident,
sentences.zh: 比如，在你经历了一场重大分手、失业或经历了真正创伤性的事件之后，

sentences.en: you probably know you should be feeling things on a deeper level.
sentences.zh: 你大概知道自己应该在更深层面上感受到一些东西。

sentences.en: You know you should be grieving or anxious, but it is like this emergency part of your body switches off and you don't necessarily know whether it would be better
sentences.zh: 你知道自己应该感到悲痛或焦虑，但你身体里仿佛有一个紧急开关被关闭了，你未必知道重新把它打开是否会更好。

sentences.en: to switch it back on again.
sentences.zh: 重新打开它是否会更好。

sentences.en: People can last like years in this state of numbness, even after the original situation is like well in the past, even after the thing is like,
sentences.zh: 人们在这种麻木的状态中可以持续好几年，甚至在最初的情况早已过去之后，甚至在事情发生很久之后——

sentences.en: even if it looks like they've eerily been coping all along, what's actually happening is that the emotions are like, they're still sitting in the emotional waiting room.
sentences.zh: 哪怕他们看起来一直都在不可思议地咬牙坚持，但实际发生的情况是，这些情绪就像是依然坐在情绪的候诊室里。

sentences.en: They are yet to be processed and they need to be processed to be moved out of that waiting room.
sentences.zh: 它们尚未被处理，而必须经过处理才能被请出那个候诊室。

sentences.en: So why are we so bad at feeling our feelings?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们在感受情绪这件事上这么差劲？

sentences.en: Obviously there's a few very clear reasons.
sentences.zh: 显然，这背后有几个非常明确的原因。

sentences.en: The biggest one being that
sentences.zh: 最主要的一个原因是：

sentences.en: processing our emotions in a helpful way was probably something that was never modeled to us as children or at any stage really by society, by our parents, by anybody.
sentences.zh: 以有益的方式处理情绪，可能从来都不是我们在孩提时代被示范过的事情，无论是在社会的任何阶段、通过父母还是任何人。

sentences.en: And so we don't have a guide on how to feel our emotions without them completely overwhelming us.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们没有一本指南教我们如何在不被情绪彻底淹没的情况下感受它们。

sentences.en: There's this, well, there was this really huge paper from like, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 这里有一个，嗯，有一篇非常庞大的论文，大概来自，我不知道，

sentences.en: 2010 that showed, especially if you have emotionally stunted parents in particular, this reduces how many different emotions people report being able to label or feel.
sentences.zh: 2010年，它表明，特别是如果你的父母情感发育受阻的话，这会减少人们报告自己能够标记或感受到的不同情绪的数量。

sentences.en: And it's highly correlated to emotional suppression in individuals themselves.
sentences.zh: 这与个体自身的情绪压抑高度相关。

sentences.en: So people couldn't name as many emotions as they actually had available to them.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们甚至无法说出他们原本可以调动的所有情绪。

sentences.en: Contrary to popular belief, emotions are also not things that we're born understanding.
sentences.zh: 与大众的普遍认知相反，情绪也不是我们生来就理解的东西。

sentences.en: Like we have to form a relationship to our emotions and that is done by modeling the people around us and seeing what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 就像我们必须与自己的情绪建立一种关系一样，这是通过模仿我们周围的人并观察他们的做法来完成的。

sentences.en: If emotions aren't shown, unless they are this like extreme thing, we don't actually get those skills.
sentences.zh: 如果情绪不被展示出来——除非它们是那种极端的事情——我们就无法真正掌握这些技能。

sentences.en: And if they, again, are only shown at their highest, most intense level, that also drives us to be a bit more avoidant of our emotions because our impression is that
sentences.zh: 而且，如果它们再次被展示时只呈现出最高、最强烈的水平，那也会驱使我们更加逃避情绪，因为我们的印象是：

sentences.en: the only way to feel our feelings is intensely and is maybe violently or is severely.
sentences.zh: 感受情绪的唯一方式就是强烈地感受，甚至可能是激烈地或严重地感受。

sentences.en: There is no moderation.
sentences.zh: 没有任何温和的缓冲。

sentences.en: Somebody's going to get hurt.
sentences.zh: 总会有人受伤。

sentences.en: And so we don't feel them at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我们干脆什么都不去感受。

sentences.en: Another reason we are bad at feeling our feelings because it feels like self-protection.
sentences.zh: 我们不擅长感受情绪的另一个原因，是因为这感觉像是一种自我保护。

sentences.en: If we don't feel sad about what happened, you know, who's to say it happened at all?
sentences.zh: 如果我们不对发生的事情感到悲伤，你知道的，谁又能说它真的发生过呢？

sentences.en: If we don't let ourselves feel angry, like then maybe the emotional impact of what we've been through will just fade away.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不允许自己感到愤怒，那么我们经历过的事情所带来的情感冲击也许就会烟消云散。

sentences.en: Like ignorance is bliss.
sentences.zh: 无知便是福。

sentences.en: That's kind of the mindset that we have unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是我们潜意识里的心态。

sentences.en: The longer we avoid the emotional consequences though, the longer we avoid, you know, the longer we avoid the origin point and we prevent ourselves from examining it.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们逃避情感后果的时间越长，我们逃避的时间——也就是我们逃避根源并阻止自己去审视它的时间就越长。

sentences.en: But there's so much research that does also show that this isn't, again, this isn't a conscious thing.
sentences.zh: 但也有大量研究表明，这同样并非出于有意识的选择。

sentences.en: Sometimes our minds will unconsciously blunt or numb our emotions for us so that we can endure hard situations and so that our immediate survival
sentences.zh: 有时，我们的头脑会无意识地为我们钝化或麻木情绪，以便我们能够忍受艰难的处境，从而使我们的即时生存

sentences.en: isn't compromised by the intensity of our sadness or the intensity of our grief, our outrage, our loneliness
sentences.zh: 不会因为悲伤的强度、悲伤的浓度、我们的愤怒、孤独感，

sentences.en: and the irrationality of those emotions sometimes.
sentences.zh: 以及这些情绪有时带来的非理性而受到损害。

sentences.en: The fact that they cause us to sometimes do things we don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 即它们有时会导致我们做出一些我们不想做的事情。

sentences.en: The issue is that off switch isn't selective.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，那个关闭按钮并不是有选择性的。

sentences.en: It's very rudimentary.
sentences.zh: 它是非常初级的。

sentences.en: It doesn't just shut down what our brain sees as compromising or bad emotions.
sentences.zh: 它不仅会关闭我们的大脑认为会带来麻烦或不好的情绪。

sentences.en: It's just going to shut down everything.
sentences.zh: 它会关闭一切。

sentences.en: Meaning that all those positive feelings we still very much want to feel get dialed down, get diluted for us also because our mind is preventing us from feeling the bad feelings.
sentences.zh: 这意味着所有那些我们依然非常渴望感受到的积极情绪也会被调低、被稀释，因为我们的大脑在阻止我们感受糟糕的情绪。

sentences.en: The good feelings come along with it.
sentences.zh: 美好的情绪也随之被一同压制了。

sentences.en: When something difficult or traumatic happens or when numerous really frustrating hard situations occur all at once, our nervous system is basically
sentences.zh: 当困难或创伤性的事情发生时，或者当许多令人沮丧的艰难状况同时发生时，我们的神经系统基本上

sentences.en: just like an overwhelmed worker.
sentences.zh: 就像一个不堪重负的工人。

sentences.en: Like it just can't cope.
sentences.zh: 它简直无法应付。

sentences.en: There's this amazing book called The Inner World of Trauma and the author of that book describes this phenomena very, very well where he says,
sentences.zh: 有一本非常棒的书叫《创伤的内心世界》（The Inner World of Trauma），这本书的作者把这种现象描述得非常非常好，他说：

sentences.en: we are all given more to experience in life than we can experience consciously.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中被赋予的体验，远比我们能够有意识地去体验的要多得多。

sentences.en: So like our brain cannot fathom everything that we have to go through.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的脑海无法完全理解我们所经历的一切。

sentences.en: Emotional numbing is one of the ways that our brain, our minds have adapted to endure it.
sentences.zh: 情绪麻木是我们的大脑、我们的思维为了忍受这一切而演化出的方式之一。

sentences.en: Remember, your brain, your mind
sentences.zh: 记住，你的大脑，你的思维

sentences.en: doesn't care if you are fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 并不在乎你是否感到充实。

sentences.en: Like at a fundamental level, it doesn't care if you are happy.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，它不在乎你是否快乐。

sentences.en: It doesn't care if you are in touch with your emotions.
sentences.zh: 它不在乎你是否与自己的情绪保持联系。

sentences.en: It just cares that you are alive.
sentences.zh: 它只在乎你是否还活着。

sentences.en: And if that means shutting down the emotional centers of the brain, so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果这意味着关闭大脑的情绪中心，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: Even if that means we don't process things fully or we never process them at all and they linger.
sentences.zh: 即使这意味着我们无法完全处理事情，或者我们永远无法处理它们，以至于它们挥之不去。

sentences.en: I think a lesser explored explanation as well is that we can also become emotionally numb and have this part of our brain shut off due to vicarious suffering and vicarious exposure
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一个较少被探讨的解释是，由于替代性痛苦以及对压力和有害事物的替代性接触，

sentences.en: to stressful and harmful things.
sentences.zh: 我们也会变得情感麻木，大脑的这一部分也会被关闭。

sentences.en: Yes, we may be enduring hard things in our lives.
